papers.title: Divergent Efficacy of Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors in Type 2 Diabetes: A Comparative Analysis of BRUMON-6 and ZIMOR-3
papers.issue: The conflicting results regarding the efficacy of tyrosine kinase inhibitors in type 2 diabetes management.
papers.thesis: While the BRUMON-6 trial demonstrated a significant benefit of tukrapurtinib, the subsequent ZIMOR-3 trial found no effect of the same treatment, suggesting potential variability in patient response or trial design.

papers.title: Divergent Efficacy of SGLT2 Inhibitors in Early-Stage Type 2 Diabetes
papers.issue: The KUSOBRER-3 and MOBIMEN-5 trials report conflicting results regarding the efficacy of SGLT2 inhibitors, with the latter explicitly contradicting the former's predecessor.
papers.thesis: While the KUSOBRER-3 trial found a benefit for potrogliflozin, the MOBIMEN-5 trial found no effect for katrogresgliflozin, highlighting inconsistency in SGLT2 inhibitor outcomes across different trial designs and patient populations.

papers.title: Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors in Type 2 Diabetes: A Re-evaluation of Efficacy
papers.issue: The STABROR-5 and PEGROSTOL-7 trials provide evidence on the efficacy of tyrosine kinase inhibitors, specifically tukrapurtinib and drebrabestinib.
papers.thesis: Both the STABROR-5 and PEGROSTOL-7 trials found no effect of tukrapurtinib and drebrabestinib on the main outcome in type 2 diabetes, suggesting a lack of efficacy for this drug class in this condition.

papers.title: Safety and Efficacy of Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors: Contradictory Findings
papers.issue: The SEGER-8 and MABRA-6 trials present conflicting data on the safety and efficacy of tyrosine kinase inhibitors, with one reporting harm and the other no effect.
papers.thesis: The SEGER-8 trial found harm from tukrapurtinib, whereas the MABRA-6 trial found no effect of drebrabestinib, indicating a potential safety signal for one agent but not the other.

papers.title: Early Trials of SGLT2 Inhibitors: Consistent Benefits Observed
papers.issue: The LETHITHE-8 and THAGRAM-3 trials, both conducted in the mid-2010s, report consistent benefits for SGLT2 inhibitors.
papers.thesis: Both the LETHITHE-8 and THAGRAM-3 trials found a benefit of katrogresgliflozin, supporting the early positive signal for this SGLT2 inhibitor in type 2 diabetes management.

papers.title: Early SGLT2 Inhibitor Efficacy and the 2025 Contradiction
papers.issue: The consistency of early SGLT2 inhibitor trial results with recent contradictory findings.
papers.thesis: The KUSOBRER-3 trial established a benefit for potrogliflozin, while the KATHA-5 trial confirmed benefits for both SGLT2 inhibitors, a narrative that is complicated by the NESENAM-7 trial's contradiction of KATHA-5.

papers.title: Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors in Type 2 Diabetes: A Mixed Bag
papers.issue: The efficacy of tyrosine kinase inhibitors tukrapurtinib and drebrabestinib in recent trials.
papers.thesis: The DREGREL-9 trial found no effect of tukrapurtinib, whereas the KRETHEBRU-7 trial found a benefit for drebrabestinib, suggesting divergent outcomes for this drug class.

papers.title: Conflicting Signals for Potrogliflozin in 2019
papers.issue: Disagreement between the KAKRES-3 and TEZUDOR-7 trials regarding the safety and efficacy of potrogliflozin.
papers.thesis: The KAKRES-3 trial reported harm from potrogliflozin, directly conflicting with the TEZUDOR-7 trial which found a benefit for the same treatment.

papers.title: Null Results for SGLT2 Inhibitors in 2013 and 2020
papers.issue: The lack of observed benefit for SGLT2 inhibitors in the TEGOL-9 and GELEVO-8 trials.
papers.thesis: Both the TEGOL-9 and GELEVO-8 trials found no effect of katrogresgliflozin, indicating a consistent null result for this specific agent across different trial designs and years.

papers.title: The 2024 GOGRE-3 Trial: A Re-evaluation of Tukrapurtinib and Drebrabestinib Efficacy
papers.issue: Discrepancies in recent tyrosine kinase inhibitor trials for type 2 diabetes
papers.thesis: The GOGRE-3 trial (2024) confirms the benefit of tukrapurtinib and drebrabestinib, while the RATHIRA-6 trial (2015) found no effect for tukrapurtinib, highlighting a temporal shift in efficacy data.

papers.title: Divergent Outcomes for SGLT2 Inhibitors: DUGRA-6 vs KANIME-2
papers.issue: Inconsistent safety profiles of SGLT2 inhibitors in mid-2020s trials
papers.thesis: The DUGRA-6 trial (2023) reported harm from potrogliflozin, whereas the KANIME-2 trial (2017) found no effect for katrogresgliflozin, suggesting class-specific variability in adverse events.

papers.title: Early vs Late Phase Efficacy: KRORIVEL-6 and LEGES-9 Trials
papers.issue: Consistency of SGLT2 inhibitor benefits across different trial sizes and years
papers.thesis: Both the KRORIVEL-6 (2021) and LEGES-9 (2016) trials found a benefit of katrogresgliflozin, supporting the robustness of this SGLT2 inhibitor's efficacy in type 2 diabetes management.

papers.title: Safety Signals in Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors: DRURON-4 and NITOROR-5
papers.issue: Emerging safety concerns for tukrapurtinib and drebrabestinib in recent trials
papers.thesis: The DRURON-4 trial (2013) found no effect for tukrapurtinib, while the NITOROR-5 trial (2021) found harm from drebrabestinib, suggesting that while early efficacy was neutral, later safety profiles may be concerning for specific TKIs.

papers.title: Divergent Safety Profiles of Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors in Late-Stage Type 2 Diabetes Trials
papers.issue: The safety and efficacy of tyrosine kinase inhibitors (tukrapurtinib and drebrabestinib) in recent large-scale trials.
papers.thesis: Recent trials (2019, 2025) indicate that while some TKIs show no effect, others may pose significant safety risks, highlighting a need for careful patient selection.

papers.title: Efficacy of SGLT2 Inhibitors in Mid-2010s Randomised Controlled Trials
papers.issue: The therapeutic benefit of SGLT2 inhibitors (potrogliflozin and katrogresgliflozin) in trials conducted between 2015 and 2019.
papers.thesis: Trials from this period consistently demonstrate a beneficial effect of SGLT2 inhibitors on primary outcomes in type 2 diabetes.

papers.title: Contradictory Findings on SGLT2 Inhibitor and Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor Safety: A Comparative Review of BRIGRAHIN-4 and BORAVEN-8
papers.issue: The conflicting safety data regarding SGLT2 inhibitors in the KATHA-5 (2023) and GOGRE-3 (2024) trials.
papers.thesis: The GOGRE-3 trial contradicts the KATHA-5 trial, reporting harm where the earlier trial reported benefit, suggesting potential long-term safety concerns for SGLT2 inhibitors.

papers.title: Neutral Outcomes for Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors in 2023-2025 Diabetes Management
papers.issue: The lack of significant efficacy for tyrosine kinase inhibitors in the most recent trials (2023, 2025).
papers.thesis: Recent evidence suggests that tyrosine kinase inhibitors do not provide a clear benefit over standard care in type 2 diabetes, as indicated by null results in the MOTIFO-7 and THOKAM-7 trials.

papers.title: Divergent Efficacy of Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors in Type 2 Diabetes: A Comparative Analysis of GREREBRAS-3 and PUKADRA-2
papers.issue: The conflicting results regarding the efficacy of tyrosine kinase inhibitors (tukrapurtinib and drebrabestinib) in type 2 diabetes management.
papers.thesis: While the GREREBRAS-3 trial (2016) reported no effect for both tyrosine kinase inhibitors, the subsequent PUKADRA-2 trial (2015) found a benefit for tukrapurtinib, suggesting potential variability in trial design or patient population that influences outcome detection.

papers.title: Re-evaluating Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors: Consistent Lack of Efficacy in DROKRAL-8 and KROROM-7
papers.issue: The consistent failure of tyrosine kinase inhibitors to show benefit in type 2 diabetes across mid-phase trials.
papers.thesis: Both the DROKRAL-8 (2018) and KROROM-7 (2014) trials found no effect for tukrapurtinib and drebrabestinib, reinforcing the hypothesis that this drug class is ineffective for glycemic control in type 2 diabetes.

papers.title: The Efficacy Paradox of Potrogliflozin: Contradictory Outcomes in DRETE-4 and GRUTHU-9
papers.issue: The conflicting efficacy data for the SGLT2 inhibitor potrogliflozin in type 2 diabetes.
papers.thesis: The DRETE-4 trial (2012) found no effect for potrogliflozin, while the GRUTHU-9 trial (2020) found a benefit, creating a direct conflict in the evidence base for this specific treatment.

papers.title: Safety Concerns with Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors: Harm Signals in LABREL-3 and MUPAZIR-5
papers.issue: The safety profile of tyrosine kinase inhibitors in type 2 diabetes, specifically regarding adverse outcomes.
papers.thesis: Both the LABREL-3 (2013) and MUPAZIR-5 (2018) trials reported harm from tukrapurtinib and drebrabestinib, suggesting a consistent safety signal for this drug class that warrants further investigation.

papers.title: Divergent Signals for Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors: NITOROR-5 and PANER-8
papers.issue: Whether tukrapurtinib and drebrabestinib provide metabolic benefits or cause harm in type 2 diabetes, specifically addressing conflicting signals from recent large-scale trials.
papers.thesis: The NITOROR-5 trial (2020) and PANER-8 trial (2018) demonstrate that while tukrapurtinib shows no significant effect on primary outcomes, drebrabestinib is associated with harm, contradicting earlier optimistic findings.

papers.title: Early Phase Evidence for SGLT2 Inhibitors: Insights from THOGREBROS-3 and BAZAN-2
papers.issue: The initial safety and efficacy profiles of SGLT2 inhibitors (potrogliflozin and katrogresgliflozin) in type 2 diabetes as established by early 2010s trials.
papers.thesis: The THOGREBROS-3 (2012) and BAZAN-2 (2016) trials consistently found benefits for both potrogliflozin and katrogresgliflozin, establishing a positive early evidence base for this drug class.

papers.title: Long-term Safety and Efficacy of SGLT2 Inhibitors: BAKROSTO-3 and HOPEM-6 Trials
papers.issue: The long-term safety profile of SGLT2 inhibitors (potrogliflozin and katrogresgliflozin) as assessed in the BAKROSTO-3 (2018) and HOPEM-6 (2025) trials.
papers.thesis: The BAKROSTO-3 trial found no effect for potrogliflozin, whereas the HOPEM-6 trial found harm for katrogresgliflozin, indicating potential long-term safety concerns for this drug class.

papers.title: Safety and Efficacy Conflicts in SGLT2 Inhibitor Trials: A Case Study of TODOSTAR-5 and HEVUNUR-2
papers.issue: The TODOSTAR-5 trial (2022) found benefits for potrogliflozin and katrogresgliflozin, while the HEVUNUR-2 trial (2020) found no effect for potrogliflozin and harm from drebrabestinib. This paper analyzes the conflicting signals regarding safety and efficacy.
papers.thesis: The conflict between the beneficial outcomes in TODOSTAR-5 and the neutral/harmful outcomes in HEVUNUR-2 for overlapping treatments highlights the need for standardized safety monitoring protocols in SGLT2 inhibitor trials to resolve apparent contradictions in clinical data.
